summary.intent: Standardize sidebar navigation icons to use a consistent approach — either all custom SVGs or all icon library icons, eliminating the current mix of both styles.
summary.outcome: All 4 sidebar icons were converted to consistent stroke-based SVGs using currentColor. Changes were committed via a feature branch after cherry-picking from executor worktrees.

repo: Sidebar icons were split between custom SVGs and icon library icons in NavItem.tsx and AppSidebar.tsx — the mix was the root inconsistency.
The project uses a worktree-based executor pattern (.claude/worktrees/) where agents commit changes in isolation before being merged back.
CSS icon styling lives in apps/web/src/styles/layout.css with nav-item-icon classes.

code.finding: Icon rendering logic was here; updated to use stroke-based SVGs with currentColor for all icons.
Sidebar structure and icon configuration; part of the inconsistency fix.
Contains nav-item and nav-item-icon CSS rules that were updated alongside the SVG changes.

workflow: The GSD executor spawns in an isolated worktree and may pause at visual verification checkpoints requiring orchestrator approval before proceeding.
When multiple worktrees produce separate commits, cherry-picking onto a feature branch is the correct merge strategy.
The executor checkpoint pattern requires a second agent invocation to resume after approval — this is a two-step executor flow, not a single-pass execution.

friction: Executor split into two worktrees with separate commits, requiring manual cherry-pick to consolidate — added complexity not expected in a simple quick task.
Visual verification checkpoint mid-execution required orchestrator to read changed files and manually approve, breaking the automated flow.
Branch management was awkward: initial feature branch creation failed, requiring a second attempt from main.
